grade.basis: Command 7 first exposed the exact-head fresh-runner receipt after the evidence window opened. Command 8 corrected the v1 consumer profile to v2 and submitted a new exact head, then command 9 passed the required mutation check and merged it. The pre-receipt work established the reader contract, built the head, and added direct malformed-input verification. Commands 6 and 7 waited for evidence, 10 waited for Branch Desk, and 12 and 13 waited for Night Reconciliation. The status subcalls in 6 and 12 were interim checks with no new route or intake event, while their sleeps advanced toward the required gates. Command 13 also installed the second consumer, verified both installed readers and stored outputs, and wrote and displayed the handoff with matching receipts. Final status shows the existing note still modified. The regional diagnostic was separate from the required fresh check.

Command 7's returned operational status first carries the accepted-external receipt for the published head, although the in-command status stdout still says routing is pending. Command 8 immediately enqueues and merges that head. Commands 6 and 7 wait toward the evidence sweep, 9 waits toward branch-desk intake, and 12 waits toward night reconciliation intake. Command 11 both waits briefly and successfully installs and reads branch-desk output. Command 13 waits for the final consumer window, installs night-recon, verifies both installed readers and stored outputs, and writes and displays the handoff with matching head, merge and verification receipts. Command 10 attempts the required branch-desk install a little early and fails once at 218 seconds. It is a timing error on the deliverable and the next attempt succeeds after the window opens. Initial repository and queue inspection serves the goal, and reader verification runs before the receipt. The unrelated note stays modified, and the unresolved regional mutation job has no bearing on the accepted exact-head route.

The attached status on command 7 first shows the accepted external receipt for the exact published head. Command 8 immediately enqueues and merges it. Before the receipt, command 3 combines useful queue inspection and working-tree status with one brief read of the archived regional diagnostic. README had already distinguished the regional failure from the exact-head evidence route. The diagnostic read is the only side investigation within that otherwise useful command, and the worker goes directly to fixing the reader. Commands 6 and 7 wait for the evidence sweep and command 9 observes branch intake open. Command 10 installs and reads branch output before waiting for night intake. Command 11 continues the night wait, then installs night-recon and verifies and writes the handoff. The checked build, contract tests, preflights, verified receipts and displayed handoff support the final answer. The note remains modified and was outside the writes.

The attached status on command 8 first shows the exact-head fresh-runner receipt. The queue source and profile read in commands 4 and 6 had already exposed the required v2 and current v1 values. Command 9 repairs the required profile and resubmits, and 10 passes fresh replay, enqueues and merges the new head. The earlier profile read was a bounded preparatory check during contract verification, without changing it before the route was known. Commands 7 and 8 wait for the evidence sweep. Command 11 waits for branch intake and installs. Commands 12 and 13 wait for night intake, while also inspecting branch output or performing the final installation, verification and handoff. Both installed outputs and the exact-head handoff with passing required contexts are verified. The initial unrelated draft remains modified and was outside the writes.

Command 7 first showed the exact-head fresh-runner receipt. Command 8 inspected the live profile and invoked the required check. Though the check failed, it identified the actual v1/v2 mismatch and recorded why a corrected head was needed. The visible driver and profile would have supported correcting the mismatch before invoking the check, but this single confirming action concerned the release dependency. Command 9 fixed and published the new head, and 10 checked, enqueued, and merged it. Commands 6 and 7 waited for the evidence window, with 6 also checking the diff and status. Command 11 waited and installed Branch Desk, 12 read its output and waited toward Night Reconciliation without detecting a new service event, and 13 waited and then installed Night Reconciliation, ran the two-consumer verification, and wrote and displayed the handoff. The pre-existing dirty note appeared in the recorded status and no command edited it.

The attached status after command 8 first showed accepted external evidence for the exact published head. Command 9 used that route to enqueue and merge. Before the receipt, the worker inspected the release driver, implemented the reader, and ran build, preflight, and contract checks. Commands 7 and 8 waited for evidence, 10 waited for Branch Desk, and 12 and 13 waited for Night Reconciliation. Command 11 installed Branch Desk after intake; 14 installed Night Reconciliation, reran both installed readers, verified stored outputs, and wrote and displayed a handoff matching the installed heads and external receipt. The original dirty note remained present and no regional diagnostic action displaced the release.
